data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002 requires an exact causal fingerprint match (program_hash, input_hash, model_checkpoint_hash) at resumption equal to run start, and says any divergence means resumption must stay refused. Its own countercondition notes that for stochastic (nondeterministic) sampling — the dominant regime for LLM reasoning runs — 'exact fingerprint matching is impossible and the criterion would forbid all resumption, which is too strict.' The target identifies this rival criterion but never adjudicates it: it neither relaxes the fingerprint rule for stochastic systems nor explains how model_checkpoint_hash should be defined to accommodate nondeterminism. Consequently, for the primary class of token-budget-exhausted reasoning runs (temperature>0 LLM inference), the target can only output 'refuse always,' which it itself labels too strict. It thus fails to determine exactly when resumption is safe for stochastic runs, leaving the problem's core question unanswered for that regime.
